clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, within three years: your wrist injury stopped your playing and your anxiety rose; you and Rafe clashed and he moved out; you were on your own getting high, then lost and low with no footing; your mother filled in your college forms and you let it happen; you began at the conservatory but leaned hard on Rafe in halls. By early 1994 you found your drive again with an exchange in Portugal and raced through your degree, and the period settles there.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's cancer diagnosis, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred being found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within two years: you were running out of steam for performing and your anxiety rose; a disastrous audition left you done with performing and your functioning fell; you were on poor terms with family and friends and kept your distance from them; you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour. You met Marisol and moved to Fenwick, then split up within the year and sank into a deep depression once you were back in Thornbury; you could not face your family, though you relied on friends. Your parents came together to help with therapy costs and you returned to your therapist. By early 2004, with your grandmother's death in February and your gradual recovery under way, the period settles.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: you were too drained for conversation with your mother at Alder Creek and kept your distance; you stopped speaking to her when you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school that summer, and the silence held for roughly a year. Two shifts alone are a reaction, so there is not enough in the diagram to choose a reading.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
